candidates.headline: SNAP enrollment drop strains local food pantries
candidates.historical_event_date_basis: The report was published Sep. 1 and describes current local pantry demand and SNAP loss in the Quad Cities service area.
candidates.geography: Rock Island, Illinois; River Bend Food Bank 23-county service area
affected_groups: children in the River Bend service area
people who lost or could not retain SNAP benefits
candidates.pressure_type: SNAP benefit access contraction and emergency food demand
candidates.supporting_passage: KWQC reports food insecurity at a four-year high across the 23-county service area, increased pantry requests, and households reporting that SNAP had stopped.
candidates.why_it_matters: The report connects benefit-access contraction to concrete increased demand on local emergency food providers.
candidates.duplicate_check: No matching headline, source, geography, or event was found in the Aug. 31 release, Sep. 7-9 artifacts, or available Sep. 4-6 retained-processing files.

candidates.headline: Worsening hunger crisis pushes North Carolina food insecurity to generational highs

candidates.headline: Texas food banks struggle amid federal cuts and increased demand
candidates.historical_event_date_basis: The report was published Sep. 3 and documents current food-bank demand, rationing, and supply pressure in Texas.
candidates.geography: Texas, including Houston, rural counties, San Antonio, Central Texas, and the Rio Grande Valley
affected_groups: families using food banks and pantries
rural households dependent on emergency food providers
candidates.pressure_type: food-bank capacity strain, supply reduction, and SNAP access pressure
candidates.supporting_passage: The Texas Tribune reports increased demand, dwindling supplies, and food-bank rationing, including reduced distribution frequency and stricter pantry limits.
candidates.why_it_matters: The report supplies concrete provider-level evidence that emergency food capacity was under pressure across multiple Texas regions.
